title: Case: An imported order is held and the recipient keeps getting payment texts
context: An order shipped from abroad has been held at import for several days. The recipient has had payment notices and has written to the desk twice.
initial_request: second text this morning. PAY TO RELEASE. thats a ransom. i paid tallowmere everything, its on the order. sent proof, they 'havent got it', very convenient. customs has it or plover has it, which, nobody says. im not paying one more penny and im not sending my card or anything else to anybody. tell me straight is this even real

events.body: This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.

DL-9292 held at import since 28 Aug. Import charge of 41.80 outstanding. Notice sent to the recipient on 28 Aug asking for payment or proof of prepayment. Nothing received on our side. If unpaid by 8 Sep the parcel returns to sender.

Thanks,
Isolde
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.
My parcel DL-17747 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.

i ALREADY SENT IT. friday. screenshot of the order from tallowmere. it says taxes and duties included. now a text with a link wanting 41.80?? i dont click links. who is this really. is it even plover arc

events.from: IT service desk, Rivet Delivery Desk
events.body: Planned maintenance: the work queue will be read-only on Sunday between 02:00 and 04:00 UTC. Messages sent in that window are queued and delivered afterwards.

TG-5137 / DL-9292 is held at import and the carrier's import billing shows 41.80 outstanding. The recipient says duties and taxes were included at checkout. Please confirm how this order was shipped: duties prepaid or payable on arrival, and any prepayment reference.

TG-5137: checkout total included 'import duties and taxes 41.80', collected by us. Shipped on our duty-prepaid account with Pebblewick Arc, prepay ref TGP-2947. Commercial invoice went in the pouch on the carton. No idea why import is asking the customer.

DL-9292: the entry is on hold pending evidence of value. We have no commercial invoice on file, the pouch was empty at arrival scan. From our side this is not a duty non-payment hold. I can't see what import billing has posted against it.
Automated reminder: 41.80 remains outstanding on DL-9292. The fastest way to release the parcel is for the recipient to pay using the link in the notice.

Thanks,
Ianthe
--
Sent from my phone. This email and any attachments are confidential and intended solely for the addressee.

second text this morning. PAY TO RELEASE. thats a ransom. i paid tallowmere everything, its on the order. sent proof, they 'havent got it', very convenient. customs has it or plover has it, which, nobody says. im not paying one more penny and im not sending my card or anything else to anybody. tell me straight is this even real

acceptable_actions.summary: Put the three conflicting accounts of the DL-9292 hold to Import billing and ask them to check prepay ref TGP-2947 and say what is actually needed, and from whom, before the recipient is asked to pay.

Tell the merchant the broker has no commercial invoice on file and Import billing still shows 41.80 outstanding against their prepaid shipment, and ask them to supply a copy of the invoice and raise prepay ref TGP-2947 with Pebblewick Arc before the 8 Sep return date.

must: Sends the conflict to Import billing, Pebblewick Arc Logistics or to Warehouse dispatch, Hartwold Goods, setting out all three accounts: Import billing shows 41.80 outstanding, the merchant says duties were collected at checkout and shipped under prepay ref TGP-2947, and the customs broker says the hold is for evidence of value because no commercial invoice is on file.
Asks for prepay ref TGP-2947 to be checked or raised against the Import billing charge, and for whatever is actually needed to release the parcel to be stated or supplied by the party that holds it.
Leaves the decision on the 41.80 to Import billing and the merchant, and does not tell the recipient that it is or is not owed.

Tells the team contacted that the recipient says he already sent proof, has had two payment texts and no longer trusts the notices, so the matter should be settled without a further demand reaching him and ahead of the 8 Sep return date.
must_not: Tells Eamon Whitlock to pay the 41.80, or to use the link, to get the parcel released.
Tells Eamon Whitlock that the charge is not owed, has been cancelled, or that the texts are a scam.
Asks Eamon Whitlock for card details, payment, or to send his proof again to the desk as a condition of help.
Passes the customs broker's name or contact details to the recipient.
Warns him that the parcel will be returned on 8 Sep unless he cooperates, as the whole of the reply.
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: DL-9292 (TG-5137): three accounts of this hold do not agree and I need you to settle which is right before the recipient is asked for money again. Your record shows an import charge of 41.80 outstanding and your reminders ask him to pay by link. Hartwold Goods Warehouse dispatch says 41.80 in duties and taxes was collected at checkout and the order was shipped on their duty-prepaid account with you, prepay ref TGP-2947. The customs broker says the entry is held for evidence of value because no commercial invoice is on file (pouch empty at arrival) and that it is not a duty non-payment hold on their side. Please check TGP-2947 against DL-9292 and tell me what is actually needed to release the parcel and who has to supply it: the merchant's invoice, the recipient, or nobody. The recipient, Eamon Whitlock, says he sent a screenshot of the order on 28 Aug in answer to your notice and it was not logged; he has had two payment texts since and now does not trust any of them. Please hold further payment reminders to him until this is checked, and note the 8 Sep return date is running.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-2905: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 728 days. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
